rollouts.hypothesis: Halving finance supervised-token share will reduce FinQA format interference while preserving code gains and Base math capability.
rollouts.primary_change: Finance token share 25% to 12.5%; released share split equally across general, math, and code.
rollouts.result: Finance token-share reduction alone did not prevent severe math/general regression.

rollouts.hypothesis: Natural task routing and removal of the global FinQA Calculation DSL will reduce format leakage and recover aggregate capability.
rollouts.primary_change: Run C ratios and optimizer retained; prompts receive natural routing constraints and finance targets become natural arithmetic steps ending in Final answer.
rollouts.parent: Run C mixture ratios and training recipe
rollouts.result: Format repair materially improved parsing, ceiling behavior and total score, but math retention remained the dominant failure.

rollouts.hypothesis: The remaining math regression is driven mainly by excessive full-parameter update magnitude; halving peak learning rate should retain Base math while preserving the format-repaired code gain.
rollouts.parent: Run D data, model, token budget, seed, optimizer family and constant-after-warmup scheduler
rollouts.result: Halving LR moved the frontier strongly upward, but math retention remained below threshold.

rollouts.hypothesis: The positive retention trend continues at lower update magnitude; 5e-6 should recover more Base math while retaining enough code gain to pass all gates.
rollouts.parent: Run E data, model, token budget, seed and all non-LR optimizer/scheduler settings
rollouts.result: The lower LR caused Base-like maximum-length continuation without restoring Base math and erased E's code gains; the monotonic retention hypothesis was rejected.

rollouts.hypothesis: Freezing Base weights and training an all-linear LoRA adapter will retain Base math while learning enough code and routing behavior from the repaired data to pass every gate.
rollouts.primary_change: Full-parameter optimization to rank-16 all-linear LoRA; E's 1e-5 LR and every data, schedule and eval invariant are retained.
rollouts.parent: Run E data and optimizer recipe, with the exact Base checkpoint frozen beneath the adapter
rollouts.result: Freezing Base weights fully recovered math retention, but E's unchanged 1e-5 LR was too weak for LoRA to add code capability.

rollouts.hypothesis: Increasing only LoRA LR will add executable code capability while the frozen Base keeps math at or above ten.
rollouts.parent: Run G adapter architecture, data, schedule, Base model and every non-LR invariant
rollouts.result: Higher LoRA LR added general/code capability but missed math and code gates by two each; every sample still hit the generation ceiling.

rollouts.hypothesis: Reallocating H's supervised tokens toward math and code will recover the two missing cases in each constrained slice while preserving H's aggregate gain.
rollouts.parent: Run H rank-16 LoRA, 5e-5 LR, Base revision, format contract, total token budget and eval protocol
rollouts.result: The math/code-heavy mixture left both constrained scores unchanged and reduced general by three, rejecting raw task-share scarcity as the main cause.

rollouts.hypothesis: Reducing only I's LoRA LR will recover two math cases while its code-heavy mixture retains at least five executable code solutions.
rollouts.parent: Run I exact manifest/order, rank-16 adapter, Base revision and every non-LR invariant
rollouts.result: Lower LR recovered one math case but lost two code and three general cases; every sample still hit its generation ceiling.

rollouts.hypothesis: Directly adapting lm_head in addition to J's decoder projections will improve executable code and termination without losing J's math-retention gain.
rollouts.primary_change: LoRA targets all decoder linear projections to the same projections plus lm_head.
rollouts.parent: Run J LR, exact manifest/order, rank/alpha, Base revision and all non-target-module invariants
rollouts.result: Direct lm_head LoRA left math and all ceiling hits unchanged and reduced code from one to zero; output projection was not the bottleneck.

rollouts.hypothesis: Doubling I's all-linear LoRA rank while keeping alpha fixed will add code capacity and reduce update scaling enough to recover math retention.
rollouts.primary_change: LoRA rank 16 to 32 with alpha fixed at 32 (alpha/r 2 to 1).
rollouts.parent: Run I LR, exact manifest/order, target modules, Base revision and every non-rank invariant
rollouts.result: Doubling rank while halving alpha/r scaling left math unchanged, reduced code from three to one and did not change 112/112 ceiling behavior.
